official.application_route: Apply directly to the Johns Hopkins neuroscience programme (neuroscience.jhu.edu/graduate/apply), naming one to four Janelia Group Leaders in the Statement of Interest; no separate Janelia application.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is stated; applicants apply through Johns Hopkins admission requirements.
official.international_eligibility: International applicants are eligible; TOEFL or IELTS scores are required for students from non-English-speaking countries, with a TOEFL waiver for those with a US or UK university degree.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Neuroscience research at HHMI Janelia Research Campus, in collaboration with Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine.
official.research_requirement: The Statement of Interest and Career Objectives must name one to four Janelia Group Leaders with whom the applicant would like to do thesis research and describe the interest in those labs; laboratory research experience is desirable.
official.duration: Multi-year PhD: one year in residence at Johns Hopkins in Baltimore followed by research years at a Janelia laboratory; the thesis defence takes place at the partner institution
official.description: The HHMI Janelia Research Campus runs fully funded graduate training programmes with the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine in which students apply directly to the Johns Hopkins neuroscience programme, spend one year in residence at Johns Hopkins, complete a summer rotation at Janelia and conduct their thesis research at a Janelia laboratory, with degrees granted by Johns Hopkins and full financial support throughout.
official.english_requirement: TOEFL or IELTS required for international graduate scholars; the TOEFL requirement can be waived for applicants who have completed, or are currently enrolled in, a degree programme at a university in the United States or United Kingdom.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate Janelia application - everything hinges on the Johns Hopkins neuroscience application and on naming one to four Janelia Group Leaders in your Statement of Interest and Career Objectives, which is the single mechanism that routes you into this programme. Funding is genuinely complete for admitted students (stipend, health insurance, programmatic travel, free housing during rotations), so the competition is about fit rather than finance. Contacting a group leader before you apply - politely, with a specific read of their work - is effectively the interview head start, and students who enter JHU without signalling Janelia interest can still join after a summer rotation, so this route is not a one-shot door.
applicant_utility.best_fit: B.S./B.A. graduates with laboratory research experience who want a fully funded neuroscience PhD and can see themselves doing thesis work in a specific Janelia lab.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply directly to the Johns Hopkins neuroscience programme; do not look for a Janelia form - none exists
Read the Janelia group leader list and name one to four labs in your Statement of Interest, describing why each fits your goals
Quantify your research experience in the Personal Statement, including months of full-time work as the guidance requests
Confirm the recommended coursework (calculus, physics, biology, general and organic chemistry) on your transcript, or address gaps in your statement
Have TOEFL or IELTS scores sent (institution code 5316) unless you qualify for the US/UK degree waiver
Secure three letters of recommendation early so the file is complete by the December 3 deadline - incomplete files are not considered
common_rejection_risks: Applying to JHU neuroscience without naming any Janelia group leaders, which removes you from this programme's pool
Naming labs whose research you clearly have not read - the statement must describe interest grounded in those labs' actual work
Letters of recommendation arriving after December 3 - the deadline explicitly includes them
A Personal Statement with no research narrative, when laboratory experience is 'desirable' and expected of competitive applicants
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Admitted students are fully supported (stipend, health insurance, programmatic travel, free housing during rotations), so the main out-of-pocket costs are application fees, test fees, relocation to Baltimore before the first stipend payment, and any personal travel beyond the funded programme and conference travel.
document_audit: The Statement of Interest and Career Objectives is a distinct document within the JHU application - it must both declare Janelia interest and list the named group leaders
TOEFL waivers apply only to applicants with a completed or in-progress degree from a US or UK university; other international applicants need scores
Graduate visas are sponsored by Johns Hopkins, not Janelia - coordinate with JHU, not the campus
alerts: The official page states the deadline as December 3 with no year, and notification by April 15 - plan around the JHU admissions calendar for the current cycle
Acceptance into the joint programme is communicated by Johns Hopkins, not Janelia, and interviews happen during the JHU recruitment visit at Janelia
Students admitted to JHU neuroscience without early Janelia interest can still transfer in after a summer rotation by agreement of the student, advisors and programme directors
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the Johns Hopkins neuroscience programme with Janelia interest and named group leaders in the Statement of Interest, submit the complete file (including three letters) by December 3, interview at Janelia during the JHU recruitment visit, receive the admission decision from JHU by early March, then spend year one at JHU with a summer rotation at Janelia before thesis research.
